selectedClaim.en: Socrates describes western and eastern bishops coming to Sardica, refusing a common conference over participation of Athanasius and Paul, then an eastern withdrawal to a separate council at Philippopolis. His 347 chronology is not adopted here;343 is a qualified editorial frame. Local reception courts are fiction, not two actual synods in the same city or a certified basilica venue.

Aquí no se adopta su cronología de 347;343 es un marco editorial cualificado. Los patios locales de recepción son ficticios, no dos sínodos reales en la misma ciudad ni sede basilical acreditada.

title.es-ES: El camino de vuelta a Alejandría

event.en: An anonymous Alexandrian chronicle dates Athanasius’ return after time in Rome and Italy to Paophi 24, rendered as 21 October 346 in the consulted edition. Socrates transmits letters concerning his recall. The following six households and local reception courts are fictional ordinary work, not the bishop’s attested entourage or entrance route.
event.es-ES: Una crónica alejandrina anónima fecha el regreso de Atanasio tras su estancia en Roma e Italia en Paofi 24, convertido en 21 de octubre de 346 por la edición consultada. Sócrates transmite cartas relativas a su retorno. Los seis hogares y patios locales de acogida que siguen son trabajo cotidiano ficticio, no el séquito acreditado ni la ruta de entrada del obispo.

historicalOutcome.en: The six fictional households reached three local hosts and the separate reception notes reached the account court. Their success changes neither Athanasius’ historical return nor the uncertainty of this local reconstruction. The next episode receives news of Constans’ death and Magnentius’ usurpation in 350; Constantius still faced a rival.
historicalOutcome.es-ES: Los seis hogares ficticios llegaron a tres anfitriones locales y las notas separadas de acogida al patio de cuentas. Su éxito no cambia el regreso histórico de Atanasio ni la incertidumbre de esta reconstrucción local. El próximo episodio recibe noticias de la muerte de Constante y la usurpación de Magnencio en 350; Constancio aún tenía un rival.

event.en: Constans was killed during Magnentius’ usurpation in 350. Constantius still faced a western rival; Magnentius’ final defeat belongs to 353. This Milan episode receives news from Gaul. The three local record stores and civilian precautions are fictional work, not an attested Milan battle, purge or confiscation order.
event.es-ES: Constante murió durante la usurpación de Magnencio en 350. Constancio aún tenía un rival occidental; la derrota final de Magnencio corresponde a 353. Este episodio de Milán recibe noticias desde la Galia. Los tres depósitos locales y las precauciones civiles son trabajo ficticio, no una batalla, purga u orden de confiscación acreditadas en Milán.

historicalOutcome.en: Three distinct fictional civilian bundles remain in their separate local stores, with a custodian at each; three reporting clerks returned after their own visits. No objective changes Constans’ death, ends the civil war in 350 or authenticates an imperial order. The next episode concerns the Milan council of 355, distinct from the Alexandria assault of 356.
historicalOutcome.es-ES: Tres legajos civiles ficticios distintos permanecen en sus depósitos locales separados, con un custodio en cada uno; tres escribientes de informe regresaron después de sus propias visitas. Ningún objetivo cambia la muerte de Constante, termina la guerra civil en 350 ni autentica una orden imperial. El próximo episodio trata del concilio de Milán de 355, distinto del asalto alejandrino de 356.

This Milan episode receives news from Gaul. The three local record stores and civilian precautions are fictional work, not an attested Milan battle, purge or confiscation order.

event.en: Later church histories describe pressure at the Milan council of 355 to support the condemnation of Athanasius, followed by exile of dissenting bishops. The sources are partisan and do not supply a neutral transcript or a securely located meeting room. This local work preserves separate context notes; it neither casts the bishops as playable counters nor lets payment decide belief or exile.
event.es-ES: Las historias eclesiásticas posteriores describen presión en el concilio de Milán de 355 para apoyar la condena de Atanasio, seguida del destierro de obispos disidentes. Las fuentes son partidistas y no ofrecen una transcripción neutral ni una sala de reunión situada con seguridad. Este trabajo local conserva notas separadas de contexto; no convierte a los obispos en fichas jugables ni permite que un pago decida creencia o destierro.

historicalOutcome.en: Separate fictional context copies and an ordinary outgoing work list reached different local stores. The council pressure and exiles remain historical narration; no goal acquits, condemns, restores or chooses a bishop. The next episode concerns the 356 nighttime assault at Alexandria, a different city and event.
historicalOutcome.es-ES: Copias ficticias separadas de contexto y una lista ordinaria de trabajo saliente llegaron a depósitos locales distintos. La presión conciliar y los destierros siguen siendo narración histórica; ningún objetivo absuelve, condena, repone ni elige a un obispo. El próximo episodio trata del asalto nocturno de 356 en Alejandría, una ciudad y un hecho distintos.

historicalBrief.en: Later church histories describe pressure at the Milan council of 355 to support the condemnation of Athanasius, followed by exile of dissenting bishops. The sources are partisan and do not supply a neutral transcript or a securely located meeting room. This local work preserves separate context notes; it neither casts the bishops as playable counters nor lets payment decide belief or exile.
historicalBrief.es-ES: Las historias eclesiásticas posteriores describen presión en el concilio de Milán de 355 para apoyar la condena de Atanasio, seguida del destierro de obispos disidentes. Las fuentes son partidistas y no ofrecen una transcripción neutral ni una sala de reunión situada con seguridad. Este trabajo local conserva notas separadas de contexto; no convierte a los obispos en fichas jugables ni permite que un pago decida creencia o destierro.

The men who brought news to our imagined workshop spoke of consent, refusal and departure. I wanted the three words to settle into one conclusion. The older copyist made me keep three lines. A clean seal cannot explain why a hand trembled.

El copista mayor me hizo conservar tres líneas. Un sello limpio no explica por qué temblaba una mano.

event.en: Athanasius describes a nighttime military assault on an Alexandrian church and his escape. An anonymous chronicle identifies Theonas and the night of Mechir 13/14 in 356; its civil conversion and the church’s exact footprint are qualified. The later transfer of churches and George’s 357 arrival are separate events. The following civilian road circuit and finite combat roster are fiction, and do not decide the bishop’s historical fate.
event.es-ES: Atanasio describe un asalto militar nocturno a una iglesia alejandrina y su huida. Una crónica anónima identifica Theonas y la noche de Mequir 13/14 en 356; se cualifican su conversión civil y la huella exacta de la iglesia. El traslado posterior de iglesias y la llegada de Jorge en 357 son hechos separados. El circuito civil de caminos y plantilla finita de combate que siguen son ficción y no deciden el destino histórico del obispo.

historicalOutcome.en: At least six of the eight original fictional civilians and one local household note reached the refuge while the marked junction remained usable. This local success neither proves a reconstructed Theonas route nor changes Athanasius’ reported escape. Later events remain separate. Next comes the western council at Ariminum in 359, with Seleucia kept off-map as a different meeting.
historicalOutcome.es-ES: Al menos seis de los ocho civiles ficticios originales y una nota local de hogares llegaron al refugio mientras el cruce señalado permanecía utilizable. Este éxito local no prueba una ruta reconstruida de Theonas ni cambia la huida relatada de Atanasio. Los hechos posteriores siguen separados. Después viene el concilio occidental de Arímino en 359, con Seleucia fuera del mapa como reunión distinta.

historicalBrief.en: Athanasius describes a nighttime military assault on an Alexandrian church and his escape. An anonymous chronicle identifies Theonas and the night of Mechir 13/14 in 356; its civil conversion and the church’s exact footprint are qualified. The later transfer of churches and George’s 357 arrival are separate events. The following civilian road circuit and finite combat roster are fiction, and do not decide the bishop’s historical fate.
historicalBrief.es-ES: Atanasio describe un asalto militar nocturno a una iglesia alejandrina y su huida. Una crónica anónima identifica Theonas y la noche de Mequir 13/14 en 356; se cualifican su conversión civil y la huella exacta de la iglesia. El traslado posterior de iglesias y la llegada de Jorge en 357 son hechos separados. El circuito civil de caminos y plantilla finita de combate que siguen son ficción y no deciden el destino histórico del obispo.

dramatizationNotice.en: The gameplay participants, records, quantities and routes are fictional local reconstruction. Later writings inform the narrators; no copy of those later books is placed inside this earlier setting. Historical persons remain in attributed narration.
dramatizationNotice.es-ES: Los participantes, registros, cantidades y rutas jugables son una reconstrucción local ficticia. Los escritos posteriores informan a los narradores; sus libros no aparecen como objetos en este escenario anterior. Las personas históricas permanecen en la narración atribuida.

text.en: Athanasius describes a nighttime military assault on an Alexandrian church and his escape. An anonymous chronicle identifies Theonas and the night of Mechir 13/14 in 356; its civil conversion and the church’s exact footprint are qualified. The later transfer of churches and George’s 357 arrival are separate events. The following civilian road circuit and finite combat roster are fiction, and do not decide the bishop’s historical fate.
text.es-ES: Atanasio describe un asalto militar nocturno a una iglesia alejandrina y su huida. Una crónica anónima identifica Theonas y la noche de Mequir 13/14 en 356; se cualifican su conversión civil y la huella exacta de la iglesia. El traslado posterior de iglesias y la llegada de Jorge en 357 son hechos separados. El circuito civil de caminos y plantilla finita de combate que siguen son ficción y no deciden el destino histórico del obispo.

text.en: The report reached us in Milan after the night was over. I was twenty-two, and the first thing I looked for was a number. Then I read the account of people trying to leave and understood how poor a beginning that was. I did not hear the doors break. I can only tell the story that reached me, and imagine the ordinary names a clerk might fear losing.
text.es-ES: El informe nos llegó a Milán después de aquella noche. Tenía veintidós años y lo primero que busqué fue una cifra. Después leí el relato de personas intentando salir y entendí lo pobre que era ese comienzo. No oí romperse las puertas. Solo puedo contar la historia que me llegó e imaginar los nombres corrientes que un escribiente temería perder.

text.en: The eight marked civilians form one fixed original group. Any six survivors can reach the southern refuge; losing a third causes main defeat. The initial registration does not freeze the first six as the only eligible people: another surviving original may still be brought. A local household note also must arrive. Keep the marked junction controlled and passable after clearing its four fixed guards, even if civilians use the western alternative. Pay 100 food/60 wood at preparation and 240 food/60 wood at refuge, once each. There are 20 initial friendly troops, no military production or free replacements, and a finite disclosed enemy roster. The source church and the bishop’s escape remain historical narration.
text.es-ES: Los ocho civiles señalados forman un único grupo original fijo. Cualesquiera seis supervivientes pueden llegar al refugio sur; perder un tercero causa derrota principal. El registro inicial no fija a los seis primeros como únicas personas elegibles: todavía puede llegar otro original superviviente. También debe llegar una nota local de hogares. Conserva el cruce señalado controlado y transitable tras despejar sus cuatro guardias fijos, incluso si los civiles usan la alternativa occidental. Paga 100 alimento/60 madera en preparación y 240 alimento/60 madera en refugio, una vez cada uno. Hay 20 tropas amigas iniciales, sin producción militar ni reemplazos gratuitos, y una plantilla enemiga finita indicada. La iglesia de la fuente y la huida del obispo siguen siendo narración histórica.

event.en: In 359 western bishops met at Ariminum, while a separate eastern council assembled at Seleucia. Later pro-Nicene accounts describe rival drafts, delegations and pressure during a prolonged gathering. They do not provide a neutral transcript or a securely located council room. This fictional local work network preserves distinct reports and supplies ordinary assistants; its success cannot determine the historical formula.
event.es-ES: En 359 los obispos occidentales se reunieron en Arímino, mientras un concilio oriental separado se congregaba en Seleucia. Relatos posteriores favorables a Nicea describen borradores rivales, delegaciones y presión durante una reunión prolongada. No ofrecen una transcripción neutral ni una sala conciliar situada con seguridad. Esta red local ficticia conserva informes distintos y abastece a ayudantes ordinarios; su éxito no determina la fórmula histórica.

historicalOutcome.en: Later accounts describe acceptance of a disputed formula under pressure, followed by continued disagreement. That outcome remains fixed. Two separate fictional assistant cohorts completed their own local returns, and a provision index reached its archive. These receipts record delivery, without certifying current residence or reproducing synodal signatures. The next act begins with Julian’s reign and changing religious policy; Seleucia and imperial journeys remain off-map.
historicalOutcome.es-ES: Relatos posteriores describen la aceptación de una fórmula disputada bajo presión, seguida de desacuerdo persistente. Ese resultado permanece fijado. Dos grupos ficticios separados de ayudantes completaron sus propios regresos locales y un índice de provisiones llegó al archivo. Los recibos registran entrega sin acreditar permanencia actual ni reproducir firmas sinodales. El siguiente acto comienza con el reinado de Juliano y cambios de política religiosa; Seleucia y los viajes imperiales siguen fuera del mapa.

en: The Winter of Divided Voices
es-ES: El invierno de las voces divididas

text.en: In 359 western bishops met at Ariminum, while a separate eastern council assembled at Seleucia. Later pro-Nicene accounts describe rival drafts, delegations and pressure during a prolonged gathering. They do not provide a neutral transcript or a securely located council room. This fictional local work network preserves distinct reports and supplies ordinary assistants; its success cannot determine the historical formula.
text.es-ES: En 359 los obispos occidentales se reunieron en Arímino, mientras un concilio oriental separado se congregaba en Seleucia. Relatos posteriores favorables a Nicea describen borradores rivales, delegaciones y presión durante una reunión prolongada. No ofrecen una transcripción neutral ni una sala conciliar situada con seguridad. Esta red local ficticia conserva informes distintos y abastece a ayudantes ordinarios; su éxito no determina la fórmula histórica.

screens.captionPolicy: split into consecutive captions without dropping qualifications; keep accents

en: Marcus speaks from received accounts and his later experience of sorting reports. He was not a witness in the Ariminum council or its imperial audiences.
es-ES: Marco habla desde relatos recibidos y su experiencia posterior de ordenar informes. No presenció el concilio de Arímino ni sus audiencias imperiales.

text.en: I was twenty-five when those accounts began reaching me. One packet smelled of damp wool; another had been wrapped so carefully that I trusted it before I had read it. My senior asked why a dry cover deserved a better hearing. I had no answer that would survive being written down. I opened two columns and sent for the provision list. Someone would still have to feed the work teams.
text.es-ES: Tenía veinticinco años cuando empezaron a llegarme aquellos relatos. Un paquete olía a lana húmeda; otro venía tan bien envuelto que confié en él antes de leerlo. Mi superior preguntó por qué una cubierta seca merecía mejor audiencia. No tenía una respuesta que resistiera al ponerla por escrito. Abrí dos columnas y pedí la lista de provisiones. Alguien tendría que alimentar a los equipos de trabajo.

event.en: After Constantius’ death, Julian entered Constantinople in December 361. Ammianus later describes decrees reopening temples and restoring sacrifice. Orders are evidence of policy, not proof that every site reopened or every resident changed belief. This fictional civic network serves ordinary local work courts without assigning religious identity to the people receiving supplies. No goal chooses, reverses or enforces an imperial creed.
event.es-ES: Tras la muerte de Constancio, Juliano entró en Constantinopla en diciembre de 361. Amiano describe después decretos que reabren templos y restablecen sacrificios. Las órdenes prueban una política, no que todos los lugares abrieran ni que todos los habitantes cambiaran de creencia. Esta red cívica ficticia atiende patios locales de trabajo cotidiano sin asignar identidad religiosa a quienes reciben provisiones. Ningún objetivo elige, revoca ni impone un credo imperial.

historicalOutcome.en: Three fictional work courts recorded their own helpers, supply allocations and local notes. These deliveries do not establish present residence, a temple’s location or religious compliance. Julian’s policy remains part of the historical account; local outcomes cannot measure everyone’s response. The next episode follows received accounts of Athanasius’ return and renewed expulsion at Alexandria, with the Persian campaign kept off-map.
historicalOutcome.es-ES: Tres patios ficticios de trabajo registraron sus propios ayudantes, asignaciones de suministros y notas locales. Las entregas no prueban permanencia actual, la ubicación de un templo ni cumplimiento religioso. La política de Juliano sigue en el relato histórico; los resultados locales no miden la respuesta de todos. El próximo episodio sigue relatos recibidos del regreso y nueva expulsión de Atanasio en Alejandría, con la campaña persa fuera del mapa.

text.en: I was twenty-seven. A porter laid a split carrying pole beside my desk. I had made the three shares add up and forgotten how far each load still had to go. He watched as I drew the routes again. I remember resenting his patience. A new reign had given me a new heading; it had not given him a sound pole.

Él miró mientras yo volvía a dibujar las rutas. Recuerdo que me irritó su paciencia. Un reinado nuevo me había dado un encabezamiento nuevo; a él no le había dado una vara entera.

event.en: In 362 Athanasius returned to Alexandria and later withdrew after Julian ordered him to leave. The emperor’s letter distinguishes return home from return to church; an anonymous Alexandrian chronicle reports local directions differently. These are interested accounts, not a neutral legal verdict. Julian’s death on the Persian expedition in 363 is a later, distant event. This local reconstruction follows fictional household work and separate working records, without making Athanasius a playable escort.
event.es-ES: En 362 Atanasio regresó a Alejandría y más tarde se retiró después de que Juliano le ordenara salir. La carta imperial distingue regreso al hogar de regreso a la iglesia; una crónica anónima alejandrina refiere instrucciones locales de otro modo. Son relatos interesados, no un veredicto jurídico neutral. La muerte de Juliano en la expedición persa de 363 es un hecho posterior y distante. Esta reconstrucción local sigue trabajo de hogares ficticios y registros separados, sin convertir a Atanasio en una escolta jugable.

historicalOutcome.en: Both fictional household cohorts completed onward journeys authorized by their own earlier reception records, and a qualified local timeline was delivered. These receipts do not trace Athanasius’ route or certify anyone’s current residence. Julian’s later death belongs to the Persian campaign, with no verified assailant supplied by the selected Ammianus passage. Its announcement at Alexandria occurred later. The next episode moves to the new orders, local opposition and further withdrawal and recall reported at Alexandria in 365–366. These are later events, not the next morning.
historicalOutcome.es-ES: Ambos grupos de hogares ficticios completaron trayectos posteriores autorizados por sus propios registros anteriores de acogida y se entregó una cronología local matizada. Los recibos no trazan el itinerario de Atanasio ni acreditan permanencia actual. La muerte posterior de Juliano pertenece a la campaña persa; el pasaje elegido de Amiano no identifica al agresor. Su anuncio en Alejandría fue posterior. El próximo episodio pasa a las nuevas órdenes, oposición local y otra retirada y regreso por orden imperial referidos en Alejandría en 365–366. Son hechos posteriores, no la mañana siguiente.

historicalNote.en: In 362 Athanasius returned to Alexandria and later withdrew after Julian ordered him to leave. The emperor’s letter distinguishes return home from return to church; an anonymous Alexandrian chronicle reports local directions differently. These are interested accounts, not a neutral legal verdict. Julian’s death on the Persian expedition in 363 is a later, distant event. This local reconstruction follows fictional household work and separate working records, without making Athanasius a playable escort.
historicalNote.es-ES: En 362 Atanasio regresó a Alejandría y más tarde se retiró después de que Juliano le ordenara salir. La carta imperial distingue regreso al hogar de regreso a la iglesia; una crónica anónima alejandrina refiere instrucciones locales de otro modo. Son relatos interesados, no un veredicto jurídico neutral. La muerte de Juliano en la expedición persa de 363 es un hecho posterior y distante. Esta reconstrucción local sigue trabajo de hogares ficticios y registros separados, sin convertir a Atanasio en una escolta jugable.

text.en: The first account said returned. I had already cleared a space in the register when the next account gave the word a different meaning. At twenty-eight I still hated crossing out a good heading. I pressed too hard and tore the thin sheet. The man beside me turned it over and started a second column. He did not pretend the first had never been written.
text.es-ES: El primer relato decía que había regresado. Ya había dejado un espacio en el registro cuando el siguiente dio otro sentido a la palabra. A los veintiocho años aún odiaba tachar un buen encabezamiento. Apreté demasiado y rasgué la hoja fina. El hombre que tenía al lado le dio la vuelta y empezó una segunda columna. No fingió que la primera nunca se hubiera escrito.

text.en: I kept the torn sheet. When news came of Julian’s death I wanted one firm sentence to close that bundle of papers. Yet I had never seen the battlefield; I knew only what the messenger had brought. I left the attacker unnamed. Years later, when another emperor’s law arrived, my handwriting had grown smaller. The gap between those headings was a part of my life, not an empty line.
text.es-ES: Guardé la hoja rasgada. Cuando llegó la noticia de la muerte de Juliano quise una frase firme para cerrar aquel legajo. Pero nunca había visto el campo de batalla; solo sabía lo que había traído el mensajero. Dejé sin nombre al agresor. Años después, cuando llegó la ley de otro emperador, mi letra se había hecho más pequeña. El espacio entre aquellos encabezamientos era parte de mi vida, no una línea vacía.

event.en: An anonymous Alexandrian chronicle reports that a renewed imperial expulsion order reached the city in 365. Supporters disputed whether it applied to Athanasius. The same account describes his secret withdrawal, a later imperial letter and his return in 366. These are a partisan account’s claims, not a neutral verdict or a located route. This episode follows an imagined local support network while the bishop’s movements remain outside player control.
event.es-ES: Una crónica alejandrina anónima refiere la llegada de una nueva orden imperial de expulsión en 365. Sus partidarios discutieron si afectaba a Atanasio. El mismo relato describe su retirada secreta, una carta imperial posterior y su regreso en 366. Son afirmaciones de un relato partidario, no un veredicto neutral ni un itinerario localizado. Este episodio sigue una red local de apoyo imaginada; los movimientos del obispo quedan fuera del control del jugador.

historicalOutcome.en: The two fictional local stations were supplied and at least four of the six original volunteers were alive at their assigned stations when the final handover completed. The chronicle separately attributes Athanasius’ return to an imperial letter and local proceedings. The player has neither caused that decision nor located his refuge. The next episode moves forward to the contested succession conventionally dated 373; the intervening years remain a narrated gap.
historicalOutcome.es-ES: Los dos puestos locales ficticios recibieron provisiones y, al completar la entrega final, al menos cuatro de los seis voluntarios originales estaban vivos en sus puestos asignados. La crónica atribuye por separado el regreso de Atanasio a una carta imperial y actuaciones locales. El jugador no ha causado esa decisión ni localizado su refugio. El siguiente episodio avanza hasta la sucesión disputada fechada convencionalmente en 373; los años intermedios siguen siendo un intervalo narrado.

No disaster-damaged building is asserted from modern ruin photographs. text.en: Register any four of the six original volunteers, all three original local supply lots and the original runner. Volunteers 1–3 have northwest station assignments; volunteers 4–6 have southeast assignments. You may keep the other two available for ordinary errands.

Los voluntarios 1–3 tienen asignado el puesto noroccidental; los 4–6, el suroriental. Puedes dejar a los otros dos disponibles para recados cotidianos.

personaReaction.en: Six willing hands are not six hands I must pin to the page.

text.en: Supply the northwest station with lots 1–2 and 160 food/80 wood; supply the southeast station with lot 3 and 100 food/100 wood. Bring the original runner to the northwest station. To complete this phase, at least four original volunteers must be alive at their individually assigned stations at the same time. Any valid four may count.
text.es-ES: Abastece el puesto noroccidental con los lotes 1–2 y 160 de alimento/80 de madera; el suroriental con el lote 3 y 100 de alimento/100 de madera. Lleva al recadero original al puesto noroccidental. Para completar esta fase, al menos cuatro voluntarios originales deben estar vivos simultáneamente en sus puestos asignados. Cuentan cuatro cualesquiera que cumplan esas condiciones.

receiptText.en: Both exact local supply shares and runner reception are recorded; a live four-person support quorum is checked before advancing. Historical deliveries alone do not preserve current staffing.
receiptText.es-ES: Quedan registradas ambas asignaciones exactas y la recepción del recadero; se comprueba un mínimo simultáneo de cuatro voluntarios presentes antes de avanzar. Las entregas pasadas no mantienen por sí solas la dotación actual.

personaReaction.en: She sent one basket by the north lane and another by the south. I had drawn only one line.

text.en: After the original runner’s own northwest reception, authorize that runner’s departure and bring the same runner alive to the southeast station. Pay 120 food and 60 wood there once. Complete the handover with any four original volunteers currently alive at their assigned stations. If too few are present, restore the quorum; earlier visits are insufficient.
text.es-ES: Tras la recepción noroccidental propia del recadero original, autoriza su salida y lleva al mismo recadero con vida al puesto suroriental. Paga allí una vez 120 de alimento y 60 de madera. Completa la entrega con cuatro voluntarios originales cualesquiera que estén vivos en ese momento en sus puestos asignados. Si faltan, restablece el mínimo; no bastan visitas anteriores.

receiptText.en: The same original runner completed the receipt-qualified onward journey, the final local share is funded, and a live quorum of four original volunteers is present at completion.

historicalBrief.en: An anonymous Alexandrian chronicle reports that a renewed imperial expulsion order reached the city in 365. Supporters disputed whether it applied to Athanasius. The same account describes his secret withdrawal, a later imperial letter and his return in 366. These are a partisan account’s claims, not a neutral verdict or a located route. This episode follows an imagined local support network while the bishop’s movements remain outside player control.
historicalBrief.es-ES: Una crónica alejandrina anónima refiere la llegada de una nueva orden imperial de expulsión en 365. Sus partidarios discutieron si afectaba a Atanasio. El mismo relato describe su retirada secreta, una carta imperial posterior y su regreso en 366. Son afirmaciones de un relato partidario, no un veredicto neutral ni un itinerario localizado. Este episodio sigue una red local de apoyo imaginada; los movimientos del obispo quedan fuera del control del jugador.

dramatizationNotice.en: The six volunteers, two stations, three supply lots, runner, bread woman, work shares and conversations are fiction. Neither station is Athanasius’ villa or a church under search. The title evokes an unlocated river mentioned by the chronicle; it does not promise a surveyed crossing. Historical months pass through narration. No playable bishop, religious fine, invented combat, tsunami hazard or authenticity claim is attached to this local work.
dramatizationNotice.es-ES: Los seis voluntarios, dos puestos, tres lotes de provisiones, recadero, mujer del pan, asignaciones y conversaciones son ficticios. Ningún puesto es la villa de Atanasio ni una iglesia registrada. El título evoca un río sin localizar mencionado por la crónica; no promete un cruce topográfico acreditado. Los meses históricos pasan mediante narración. No hay obispo jugable, multa religiosa, combate inventado, peligro de tsunami ni pretensión de autenticidad en este trabajo local.

reports.

text.en: The woman who brought our bread waited while I sharpened a reed. She had counted six willing hands in the neighborhood; I had written down four places that needed filling. For a moment I thought we were speaking about the same thing. Then she asked who would carry the next basket if every willing hand stayed at a door. The Alexandrian reports lay beside my elbow. They told me where a bishop was said to have gone. They did not tell me how this woman would get through her morning.
text.es-ES: La mujer que nos traía el pan esperó mientras yo afilaba una caña. Había contado seis manos dispuestas en el vecindario; yo había anotado cuatro puestos que necesitaban cubrirse. Por un instante creí que hablábamos de lo mismo. Entonces preguntó quién llevaría la siguiente cesta si todas las manos dispuestas se quedaban ante una puerta. Los relatos alejandrinos descansaban junto a mi codo. Decían adónde se suponía que había ido un obispo. No decían cómo iba a sacar adelante aquella mujer su mañana.

text.en: Six original volunteers have fixed station assignments: 1–3 northwest, 4–6 southeast. Any four currently at their own stations count at the two main checkpoints, so 3+1, 2+2 and 1+3 work. Visiting earlier does not count after leaving. Staffing is checked at completion, not continuously between phases. The runner must first reach northwest, then depart under that own receipt and arrive southeast. Three supply lots have fixed 2/1 destinations. Every main destination and exact cost remains visible on all difficulties.
text.es-ES: Los seis voluntarios originales tienen puestos fijos: 1–3 noroeste, 4–6 sureste. En los dos controles principales cuentan cuatro cualesquiera presentes en su propio puesto: valen 3+1, 2+2 y 1+3. Visitar antes no cuenta después de marcharse. La dotación se comprueba al completar, no continuamente entre fases. El recadero debe llegar primero al noroeste, salir bajo su propio recibo y llegar al sureste. Los tres lotes tienen destinos fijos 2/1. Todos los destinos y costes principales son visibles en las tres dificultades.

text.en: The two fictional local stations were supplied and at least four of the six original volunteers were alive at their assigned stations when the final handover completed. The chronicle separately attributes Athanasius’ return to an imperial letter and local proceedings. The player has neither caused that decision nor located his refuge. La crónica atribuye por separado el regreso de Atanasio a una carta imperial y actuaciones locales. El jugador no ha causado esa decisión ni localizado su refugio. El siguiente episodio avanza hasta la sucesión disputada fechada convencionalmente en 373; los años intermedios siguen siendo un intervalo narrado.

text.en: Before she left, the bread woman turned the reed in my fingers and cut its end properly. It had been scraping all morning. I had thought the fault was in my hand. On the little account I left two names free for other work. The great account from Alexandria would be copied again when the next news arrived. I did not know how many quiet mornings lay between those pages.
text.es-ES: Antes de marcharse, la mujer del pan giró la caña entre mis dedos y cortó bien la punta. Había estado raspando toda la mañana. Yo creía que el fallo estaba en mi mano. text.en: Athanasius died in the period conventionally dated 373. An anonymous chronology names Peter as his successor; Socrates and Sozomen describe imperial intervention, Peter’s imprisonment and flight to Rome, and Lucius’ possession of the churches. These later Nicene accounts have their own commitments. Socrates’ consular synchronism conflicts with the adopted year. The playable withdrawal concerns ordinary fictional households, not Peter’s escape or a battle attested at these street corners.
text.es-ES: Atanasio murió en el periodo fechado convencionalmente en 373. Una cronología anónima nombra a Pedro como sucesor; Sócrates y Sozomeno describen intervención imperial, prisión y huida de Pedro a Roma y posesión de las iglesias por Lucio. Son relatos nicenos posteriores con compromisos propios. El sincronismo consular de Sócrates contradice el año adoptado. La retirada jugable afecta a hogares ficticios cotidianos, no a la fuga de Pedro ni a una batalla documentada en estas esquinas.

text.en: My older colleague had gone home to a sick father, and his chair stood empty beside mine. I kept leaving a second cup there. When the Alexandrian report arrived, I read the names of the men who were said to hold a church and then looked at that cup. Habit had supplied a person whom the room could not supply. In the ordinary withdrawal we imagine here, I want a place ready before I put another name against it.
text.es-ES: Mi compañero mayor había vuelto a casa para cuidar a su padre enfermo, y su silla quedó vacía junto a la mía. Yo seguía dejando allí una segunda taza. Cuando llegó el relato alejandrino, leí los nombres de quienes supuestamente poseían una iglesia y miré aquella taza. La costumbre había puesto una persona que la habitación no podía aportar. En la retirada cotidiana que imaginamos aquí, quiero que haya sitio antes de escribir otro nombre.

event.en: In 378 the Roman army suffered a major defeat near Hadrianopolis and Valens died. Ammianus gives alternative accounts of his death and describes scattered survivors. The exact battlefield remains disputed. This episode imagines one small withdrawal in the real regional landscape; it does not reconstruct an attested formation or reverse the defeat. The later siege of the city is a separate event.
event.es-ES: En 378 el ejército romano sufrió una gran derrota cerca de Adrianópolis y Valente murió. Amiano ofrece versiones alternativas de su muerte y describe supervivientes dispersos. La localización exacta de la batalla sigue discutida. Este episodio imagina una pequeña retirada en el paisaje regional real; no reconstruye una formación documentada ni invierte la derrota. El asedio posterior de la ciudad es un hecho distinto.

historicalOutcome.en: The fictional foot and mounted groups completed their local withdrawal to a provisioned area outside the city. The Roman defeat and Valens’ death remain unchanged. No city gate, cottage or exact battlefield has been identified by this map. The next episode moves to Sirmium in 379 and the appointment of Theodosius; the local survivors do not cause that imperial decision.
historicalOutcome.es-ES: Los grupos ficticios de a pie y montados completaron su retirada local hasta una zona abastecida fuera de la ciudad. La derrota romana y la muerte de Valente permanecen. El mapa no identifica puerta urbana, casa ni campo de batalla exactos. El siguiente episodio pasa a Sirmio en 379 y al nombramiento de Teodosio; los supervivientes locales no causan esa decisión imperial.

selectedClaim.en: The Roman army was defeated near Hadrianopolis in 378 and Valens died. Ammianus preserves conflicting death accounts and describes scattered survivors. Their local escape does not reverse the defeat, and survival did not guarantee admission to the city.
selectedClaim.es-ES: El ejército romano fue derrotado cerca de Adrianópolis en 378 y Valente murió. Amiano conserva versiones distintas de su muerte y describe supervivientes dispersos. Su fuga local no invierte la derrota, y sobrevivir no garantizaba entrar en la ciudad.

mapPlan.terrainInstructions: Real Edirne-region local frame northeast of the modern city, a fictional withdrawal sector rather than a battlefield-location proposal. The modern city locator26.5556,41.6769is off map southwest; do not draw a certified ancient gate or inside-city refuge. Separateadrianople378profile from324Hebrus ferry geography. Use existing modern Copernicus DSM for qualified regional relief: northern and eastern uplands, lower west/central/southwest corridors, southern shoulder rising again. Blue on the research color plot means lower elevation, not water. Do not flatten all400tiles or promote modern vegetation/buildings into378terrain. No compulsory Hebrus/Tundzha/Arda crossing or invented ancient bridge. Exact378microchannels, dry-ground margins, tracks and receiving surfaces remain unverified; check every full-width corridor and grade before materialization. Native height0–7band candidate is separately documented, not approved terrain. Northern foot detour versus central exposed passage must differ in actual route length, slopes and exposure. The schematic polylines and sampled DSM are not surveyed roads or safe native paths. Retain useful safe finite banks west/southwest outside full hostile acquisition/range/leash envelopes; do not put a main foot origin or receiver inside an attack radius. No ring of hostile wagons, Valens cottage, Gothic cultural caricature or miniature replica of the entire battle.

text.en: Regroup any four of six original foot stragglers and any two of four original mounted scouts. Keep those separate minimums alive throughout. A third loss in either original group causes main defeat. All fourteen supporting troops are finite; none can substitute for a main original.
text.es-ES: Reagrupa a cuatro cualesquiera de los seis rezagados originales a pie y dos cualesquiera de los cuatro exploradores montados originales. Conserva vivos ambos mínimos por separado durante todo el escenario. Una tercera baja en cualquiera de los grupos originales causa derrota principal. Las catorce tropas de apoyo son finitas; ninguna sustituye a un original principal.

receiptText.en: Both original groups are registered without spending resources or selecting a frozen first quorum.
receiptText.es-ES: Ambos grupos originales quedan registrados sin gasto de recursos ni fijar un primer grupo inmutable.

personaReaction.en: I will not turn a permitted loss into a number somebody ought to supply.
personaReaction.es-ES: No convertiré una pérdida admisible en una cifra que alguien deba aportar.

text.en: At one checkpoint, have any four living original foot stragglers currently at the western rally and any two living original mounted scouts currently at the central rally. The riders may fight but must survive. Move the foot group along the northern relief or the exposed central passage. This is a simultaneous muster check, not a continuous hold or enemy-kill quota.
text.es-ES: En una misma comprobación, reúne a cuatro rezagados originales a pie vivos y presentes en el punto occidental y dos exploradores montados originales vivos y presentes en el punto central. Los jinetes pueden combatir, pero deben sobrevivir. Lleva al grupo a pie por la alternativa norte o el paso central expuesto. Es una reunión simultánea, no una defensa continua ni una cuota de enemigos muertos.

receiptText.en: The separate foot and mounted quorums are currently at their different rally checkpoints. This receipt requires no ongoing residence once latched.
receiptText.es-ES: Los mínimos separados a pie y montado están presentes en sus distintos puntos de reunión. Este recibo no exige permanencia continua después de fijarse.

personaReaction.en: The mounted men are not markers to leave behind when the column moves.
personaReaction.es-ES: Los jinetes no son señales que se dejan atrás al marchar la columna.

text.en: Withdraw both groups to the southwest off-city reception ground. Complete with any four original foot stragglers and any two original mounted scouts alive/currently present there, and pay 180 food/80 wood once at that receiver. An old visit, dead actor, supporting soldier or optional traveler cannot substitute. The central rally no longer needs staffing.
text.es-ES: Retira ambos grupos hasta el lugar de acogida suroccidental fuera de la ciudad. Completa con cuatro rezagados originales a pie y dos exploradores montados originales vivos y presentes allí, y paga una vez 180 de alimento/80 de madera en ese receptor. No valen una visita anterior, un actor muerto, un soldado de apoyo ni un viajero opcional. El punto central ya no necesita personal.

receiptText.en: Both original groups are now at the provisioned off-city receiver. No gate was opened and no historical battle was won.
receiptText.es-ES: Ambos grupos originales están ahora en la acogida abastecida fuera de la ciudad. No se ha abierto una puerta ni ganado una batalla histórica.

personaReaction.en: There is no complete army in this little muster. There are people who have come away.
personaReaction.es-ES: No hay un ejército completo en esta pequeña reunión. Hay personas que han logrado marcharse.

historicalBrief.en: In 378 the Roman army suffered a major defeat near Hadrianopolis and Valens died. Ammianus gives alternative accounts of his death and describes scattered survivors. The exact battlefield remains disputed. This episode imagines one small withdrawal in the real regional landscape; it does not reconstruct an attested formation or reverse the defeat. The later siege of the city is a separate event.
historicalBrief.es-ES: En 378 el ejército romano sufrió una gran derrota cerca de Adrianópolis y Valente murió. Amiano ofrece versiones alternativas de su muerte y describe supervivientes dispersos. La localización exacta de la batalla sigue discutida. Este episodio imagina una pequeña retirada en el paisaje regional real; no reconstruye una formación documentada ni invierte la derrota. El asedio posterior de la ciudad es un hecho distinto.

dramatizationNotice.en: The six foot stragglers, four mounted scouts, fourteen supporting troops, local opponents, rally areas, payments, routes and boy’s story are invented. The scouts may fight using later-certified native proxies but are not historical cavalry units. Main originals have normal initial native health; no invented wound or healing bonus is silently simulated. There is no emperor rescue, corpse search, wagon-ring capture, mandatory sacrifice, religious guilt or guaranteed city admission. The survival thresholds are gameplay margins, not Ammianus’ army-wide casualty estimate.
dramatizationNotice.es-ES: Los seis rezagados a pie, cuatro exploradores montados, catorce tropas de apoyo, adversarios locales, áreas de reunión, pagos, rutas e historia del niño son inventados. Los exploradores podrán combatir con representantes nativos acreditados después, pero no son unidades históricas de caballería. Los originales principales tienen salud nativa inicial normal; no se simula en silencio una herida ni bonificación curativa. No hay rescate imperial, búsqueda de cadáver, captura de círculo de carros, sacrificio obligatorio, culpa religiosa ni entrada urbana garantizada. Los mínimos de supervivencia son márgenes jugables, no la estimación de bajas del ejército de Amiano.

hard.basis: static feasibility estimate; native calibration and fun/playability assessment pending
hard.difficultyLevers: 6gatherers; finite6mounted/10infantry/6ranged hostiles. More mounted/ranged pressure makes scout survival, support allocation, spacing and withdrawal route choices stricter. No hidden clock, production, mandatory secondary, casualty sacrifice or compulsory conquest. Demonstrate this in AoE2; worker count and longer waits alone do not pass.
hard.movementPolicy: native movement/health/damage unchanged; no difficulty cheats

playstyles.costOfOpportunity: Send foot originals around the longer northern relief while concentrating more support near the mounted central muster; allocate enough escort to the long column. Both different live checkpoints still need simultaneous presence.

Bring more of the finite force through the exposed central route, then separate foot west from mounted central for the checkpoint. Shorter schematic travel trades against mounted/ranged pressure; optional travelers may join without replacing originals.

Stage foot originals west/southwest and choose the southern supply shoulder for the mounted withdrawal aftero2, versus the western exit. Trade/repair can save gathering but cost escort allocation, travel and finite50W/50G. All portfolios can combine.

gameplayIdentity.problem: Withdraw a foot group and a usable mounted scout group through different simultaneous rally checkpoints, then reunite both at one off-city receiver. Mounted originals must also leave; the rear component is not a sacrifice objective.
gameplayIdentity.decision: Long northern foot approach with concentrated central support versus exposed central concentration followed by separation. After muster choose direct western withdrawal or southern supply detour. Main military force is finite and unreplaced.
gameplayIdentity.densityPlan: Eight regional grounds with finite useful banks, two staged approaches and a rising southern shoulder. Survey modern DSM cross-sections; do not draw identical flat corridors. Measure actual native route lengths and idle intervals; a huge empty detour cannot pass playability.
gameplayIdentity.replay: Any4of6foot and2of4mounted originals may satisfy each checkpoint; no first quorum is frozen. Change force split, foot route, mounted final route and secondary portfolio. No narrative historical reversal.
gameplayIdentity.historicalBoundary: All local participants, opposing patrols and destinations are licensed fiction after a fixed Roman defeat; no source casualty ratio or tactical direction is inferred from those counts.

oppositionPlan.historicalPolicy: Finite invented local opposition after a fixed defeat; not the historical Gothic/Alan army, religious party or troop roster.
oppositionPlan.worldSelectionPolicy: Only selected initial IDs instantiate; unused maximum group members absent.
oppositionPlan.engagementPolicy: Initial hostile groups at easternhub7. Proposed bounded central/eastern encounter sector lon26.676–26.750,lat41.772–41.814may contest centralhub3and the exposed route. This is a design limit, not an implemented AI polygon. Audit actor offsets, acquisition, projectile range and every leash turnaround with native proxies. OriginsNE/N, west rally, southwest reception, southern supplies and northern relief must remain outside the complete hostile envelope. No global pursuit, idle base attack, mapwide target memory or enemy reinforcements. Four original mounted scouts plus14supporting troops are the whole friendly combat force; no military production/replacement. No mandatory kill count or city assault.

stateMachine.terminalPriority: defeat first; close side rewards; one terminal latch

text.en: In 378 the Roman army suffered a major defeat near Hadrianopolis and Valens died. Ammianus gives alternative accounts of his death and describes scattered survivors. The exact battlefield remains disputed. This episode imagines one small withdrawal in the real regional landscape; it does not reconstruct an attested formation or reverse the defeat. The later siege of the city is a separate event.
text.es-ES: En 378 el ejército romano sufrió una gran derrota cerca de Adrianópolis y Valente murió. Amiano ofrece versiones alternativas de su muerte y describe supervivientes dispersos. La localización exacta de la batalla sigue discutida. Este episodio imagina una pequeña retirada en el paisaje regional real; no reconstruye una formación documentada ni invierte la derrota. El asedio posterior de la ciudad es un hecho distinto.

text.en: I had been teaching the neighbor’s boy to count with pebbles. He liked to stand the fallen ones up again and begin another army. When the news came, he asked whether we could do that with these men. I had an answer about numbers ready, and stopped before saying it. I know nothing of a soldier’s last step in that field. The little withdrawal we imagine must leave room for those still able to take another.
text.es-ES: Estaba enseñando a contar al hijo del vecino con piedrecitas. Le gustaba levantar las caídas y formar otro ejército. Al llegar la noticia, preguntó si podíamos hacer lo mismo con aquellos hombres. Tenía preparada una respuesta sobre números y me detuve antes de decirla. No sé nada del último paso de un soldado en aquel campo. La pequeña retirada que imaginamos debe dejar sitio a quienes aún puedan dar otro.

text.en: The six foot stragglers, four mounted scouts, fourteen supporting troops, local opponents, rally areas, payments, routes and boy’s story are invented. The scouts may fight using later-certified native proxies but are not historical cavalry units. Main originals have normal initial native health; no invented wound or healing bonus is silently simulated. There is no emperor rescue, corpse search, wagon-ring capture, mandatory sacrifice, religious guilt or guaranteed city admission. The survival thresholds are gameplay margins, not Ammianus’ army-wide casualty estimate.
text.es-ES: Los seis rezagados a pie, cuatro exploradores montados, catorce tropas de apoyo, adversarios locales, áreas de reunión, pagos, rutas e historia del niño son inventados. Los exploradores podrán combatir con representantes nativos acreditados después, pero no son unidades históricas de caballería. Los originales principales tienen salud nativa inicial normal; no se simula en silencio una herida ni bonificación curativa. No hay rescate imperial, búsqueda de cadáver, captura de círculo de carros, sacrificio obligatorio, culpa religiosa ni entrada urbana garantizada. Los mínimos de supervivencia son márgenes jugables, no la estimación de bajas del ejército de Amiano.

text.en: Foot originals: northeast gathering, then west rally, finally southwest off-city reception. Mounted originals: north gathering, then central rally, finally the same southwest receiver. At the middle checkpoint four foot originals west and two mounted originals central must be present simultaneously. Then release both stations and withdraw; riders are not disposable. Main destinations and both major foot approaches are known without optional scouting. Only the local pressure sector can pursue; no emperor, city gate, compulsory river crossing or enemy-kill total is a main objective.

En la comprobación intermedia deben coincidir cuatro originales a pie al oeste y dos montados en el centro. Después abandona ambos puestos y retírate; los jinetes no son prescindibles. Los destinos y ambos grandes accesos a pie se conocen sin reconocimiento opcional. Solo persigue el sector local de presión; emperador, puerta urbana, cruce fluvial obligatorio y cifra de enemigos muertos no son objetivos principales.

event.en: In 379 Gratian appointed Theodosius as a fellow emperor at Sirmium and shared responsibility for the war after Valens’ death. Later church historians praised that choice from their own religious positions; their accounts do not show an immediate religious settlement everywhere. This episode imagines a small local supply assembly in the Sirmium region. Its participants and departure window are fiction, and their work does not cause the imperial appointment.
event.es-ES: En 379 Graciano nombró a Teodosio emperador asociado en Sirmio y compartió la responsabilidad de la guerra tras la muerte de Valente. Historiadores eclesiásticos posteriores elogiaron la elección desde sus propias posiciones religiosas; sus relatos no demuestran un acuerdo religioso inmediato en todas partes. El episodio imagina una pequeña reunión local de provisiones en la región de Sirmio. Sus participantes y plazo de salida son ficticios, y su trabajo no causa el nombramiento imperial.

historicalOutcome.en: The fictional three-post assembly met its local preparation window, and the same three supply units completed their authorized onward journeys with a live reception of six original crew members. Theodosius’ appointment remains a historical event independent of that work. The next episode moves to Thessalonica in 380 and the imperial constitution and its reception. The interval is narrated; this local map does not contain the road between the two cities or finish the campaign.
historicalOutcome.es-ES: La reunión ficticia de tres puestos cumplió su plazo local de preparación, y las mismas tres unidades de provisiones completaron sus trayectos autorizados con seis miembros originales del equipo presentes y vivos en la recepción. El nombramiento de Teodosio sigue siendo un hecho histórico independiente de ese trabajo. El próximo episodio pasa a Tesalónica en 380 y a la constitución imperial y su recepción. El intervalo se narra; este mapa local no contiene el camino entre ambas ciudades ni termina la campaña.

text.en: Before the visible preparation clock expires, register at least six of eight original crew and all three supply units. Deliver units 1, 2 and 3 to west, central and east respectively and keep them there for this check. Pay once: west, 90 food and 60 wood; central, 70 food and 80 wood; east, 80 food and 40 wood. Total: 240 food and 180 wood. At that same check place at least two different original crew at each post. No person can occupy two separated posts.
text.es-ES: Antes de que venza el reloj visible, registra al menos seis de ocho miembros originales del equipo y las tres unidades de provisiones. Entrega las unidades 1, 2 y 3 al oeste, centro y este, respectivamente, y mantenlas allí para esta comprobación. Paga una vez: oeste, 90 de alimento y 60 de madera; centro, 70 y 80; este, 80 y 40. Total: 240 de alimento y 180 de madera. En esa misma comprobación sitúa al menos dos miembros originales distintos en cada puesto. Nadie puede ocupar dos puestos separados.

receiptText.en: All three distinct supply units are at their assigned posts, all three local shares are paid, and three separate live pairs are ready before expiry. The preparation clock now stops; all posts may be left.
receiptText.es-ES: Las tres unidades distintas están en sus puestos asignados, las tres asignaciones locales están pagadas y hay tres parejas vivas separadas preparadas antes del vencimiento. El reloj de preparación se detiene; ya se pueden abandonar los puestos.

personaReaction.en: I had spoken of setting things in order. She handed me the loose end and waited.
personaReaction.es-ES: Yo había hablado de poner las cosas en orden. Ella me tendió el cabo suelto y esperó.

text.en: After each supply unit’s own earlier reception, observe its authorized departure and bring the same three units alive to the northeastern dispatch ground. Assemble any six original crew there at the final check. Pay 120 food 80 wood once. All three supply units must still be alive and present. Preparation has ended; this final phase has no deadline.
text.es-ES: Tras la recepción anterior propia de cada unidad de provisiones, observa su salida autorizada y lleva las mismas tres con vida al despacho nororiental. Reúne allí a seis miembros originales cualesquiera para la comprobación final. Paga una vez 120 de alimento 80 de madera. Las tres unidades de provisiones deben seguir vivas y presentes. La preparación ha terminado; esta fase final no tiene plazo.

receiptText.en: The three original supply units completed their own receipt-qualified departures and arrive together with six live original crew. The dispatch share is paid once.
receiptText.es-ES: Las tres unidades originales completaron sus salidas condicionadas a sus propios recibos y llegan juntas con seis miembros originales vivos. La asignación de despacho se paga una vez.

personaReaction.en: I held the cloth while she finished. For once, my hands had arrived before my advice.
personaReaction.es-ES: Sostuve la tela mientras ella terminaba. Por una vez, mis manos habían llegado antes que mis consejos.

dramatizationNotice.en: The eight crew members, three supply units, posts, working costs, departure window and family scene are invented. The clock measures only preparation after the briefing is accepted: 20, 16 or 12 game minutes. It is not a reported imperial ultimatum, ancient date, attack, flood or historical troop count. No enemy, siege, emperor escort, religious test or purchase of the crown is playable. Supply-unit identities represent an abstract local consignment; no unsupported carried resource inventory is claimed.
dramatizationNotice.es-ES: Los ocho miembros del equipo, tres unidades de provisiones, puestos, costes de trabajo, plazo de salida y escena familiar son inventados. El reloj mide solo la preparación tras aceptar las instrucciones: 20, 16 o 12 minutos de juego. No es un ultimátum imperial documentado, fecha antigua, ataque, inundación ni cifra histórica de tropas. No se juega contra enemigos, un asedio, una escolta imperial, una prueba religiosa ni una compra de la corona. Las identidades de provisiones representan una remesa local abstracta; no se afirma un inventario de recursos transportados que el adaptador no implemente.

playstyles.costOfOpportunity: Split six crew into three pairs immediately, keep two flexible originals and send all three consignments along distinct approaches. Gather operating costs directly; surveying is optional and all destinations are disclosed.

Route an early repair allocation via southwest to reduce required operating gathering, while dispatching central/eastern pairs in parallel. Spending50Wbefore main payment competes with the preparation window. Aid can wait until phase2.

Send the trader with the eastern movement and decide whether gathering the hard profile’s missing gold is worth its finite supply benefit. After staging, combine eastern dispatch, guide and voluntary wayfarers; no secondary is necessary to beat the clock.

gameplayIdentity.problem: Prepare three individually assigned consignments and three simultaneous two-person stations from the SAME eight flexible originals before a visible, explicitly fictional readiness window ends; then release staging and dispatch a real causal onward column.
gameplayIdentity.decision: Three parallel pair assignments versus early western repair or eastern trade; choose route/worker order and leave optional care until untimed dispatch. Unlike the previous withdrawal, no enemies or fixed foot/mounted cohort exist.
gameplayIdentity.densityPlan: Eight local grounds, seven independent optional tasks, two dispatch alternatives and finite operating-bank candidates near both circuits. Exact ancient dry surfaces, native resource footprints and actor packing remain gates. Empty travel and an impossible clock do not pass.
gameplayIdentity.replay: At least2520minimal three-pair assignments from eight originals before staging;28possible six-person final subsets. Counts are combinatorics, not2520certified game strategies. Supply units retain their own distinct post receipts and onward identities.
gameplayIdentity.historicalBoundary: The imperial accession is already fixed in narration. All work groups, shares and clocks are fiction. No alleged local379battle, flood, mandatory baptism or causally purchased imperial appointment.
gameplayIdentity.approvalGate: No playability approval until all-skip/all-complete/three-portfolio runs at each difficulty show a viable clock, useful choices, finite investments and recovery, with native time/route/worker evidence.

text.en: In 379 Gratian appointed Theodosius as a fellow emperor at Sirmium and shared responsibility for the war after Valens’ death. Later church historians praised that choice from their own religious positions; their accounts do not show an immediate religious settlement everywhere. This episode imagines a small local supply assembly in the Sirmium region. Its participants and departure window are fiction, and their work does not cause the imperial appointment.
text.es-ES: En 379 Graciano nombró a Teodosio emperador asociado en Sirmio y compartió la responsabilidad de la guerra tras la muerte de Valente. Historiadores eclesiásticos posteriores elogiaron la elección desde sus propias posiciones religiosas; sus relatos no demuestran un acuerdo religioso inmediato en todas partes. El episodio imagina una pequeña reunión local de provisiones en la región de Sirmio. Sus participantes y plazo de salida son ficticios, y su trabajo no causa el nombramiento imperial.

en: Marcus is about forty-five. He receives the news in his invented clerical life at Constantinople, without attending the proclamation at Sirmium. His coat, sister and conversation belong to his fictional biography.
es-ES: Marco tiene unos cuarenta y cinco años. Recibe la noticia durante su vida administrativa inventada en Constantinopla, sin asistir a la proclamación en Sirmio. Su capa, hermana y conversación pertenecen a su
biografía ficticia.

text.en: My sister was turning the worn edge of my winter cloak when the news reached us. I began to explain what the new emperor would have to mend. She held up my sleeve and asked whether I intended to help with this smaller task first. I had not been in Sirmium; I knew the appointment only through the news that had reached us. I could offer a good opinion more quickly than I could thread her needle.
text.es-ES: Mi hermana estaba volviendo el borde gastado de mi capa de invierno cuando llegó la noticia. Empecé a explicar lo que tendría que remendar el nuevo emperador. Ella levantó mi manga y preguntó si pensaba ayudar primero con aquella tarea más pequeña. No había estado en Sirmio; solo conocía el nombramiento por la noticia que nos había llegado. Podía ofrecer una buena opinión más deprisa de lo que era capaz de enhebrarle la aguja.

Later I wore it to hear a new law read, and felt the ridge of her stitching under my thumb. I hoped the ruler would bring order. The hope was mine; it did not tell me how another household would receive his words.

event.en: On 27 February 380 a constitution was issued at Thessalonica in the names of Gratian, Valentinian and Theodosius. Its heading addresses the people of Constantinople. It prescribes the faith associated with Damasus of Rome and Peter of Alexandria and threatens those it classifies as dissenters. A prescription is not evidence of immediate acceptance or uniform enforcement. This reconstruction follows fictional local preparation and handovers; the distant addressee remains outside the map.
event.es-ES: El 27 de febrero de 380 se emitió en Tesalónica una constitución en nombre de Graciano, Valentiniano y Teodosio. Su encabezamiento se dirige al pueblo de Constantinopla. Prescribe la fe asociada con Dámaso de Roma y Pedro de Alejandría y amenaza a quienes clasifica como disidentes. Una prescripción no demuestra aceptación inmediata ni cumplimiento uniforme. Esta reconstrucción sigue preparativos y entregas locales ficticios; el destinatario distante permanece fuera del mapa.

historicalOutcome.en: Two fictional local products reached different receiving courts, and both original couriers returned on their own recorded handovers. Those local receipts establish neither delivery to Constantinople nor compliance by its inhabitants. The law remains a historical prescription with a named addressee, not a count of converted people. The next episode moves to the separately reported arrival and church-possession changes at Constantinople in November 380.
historicalOutcome.es-ES: Dos productos locales ficticios llegaron a patios receptores distintos y ambos mensajeros originales regresaron tras sus propias entregas registradas. Esos recibos locales no acreditan llegada a Constantinopla ni cumplimiento por sus habitantes. La ley sigue siendo una prescripción histórica con destinatario expreso, no un recuento de conversiones. El siguiente episodio pasa a la llegada y los cambios de posesión de iglesias referidos por separado en Constantinopla en noviembre de 380.

historicalBrief.en: On 27 February 380 a constitution was issued at Thessalonica in the names of Gratian, Valentinian and Theodosius. Its heading addresses the people of Constantinople. It prescribes the faith associated with Damasus of Rome and Peter of Alexandria and threatens those it classifies as dissenters. A prescription is not evidence of immediate acceptance or uniform enforcement. This reconstruction follows fictional local preparation and handovers; the distant addressee remains outside the map.
historicalBrief.es-ES: El 27 de febrero de 380 se emitió en Tesalónica una constitución en nombre de Graciano, Valentiniano y Teodosio. Su encabezamiento se dirige al pueblo de Constantinopla. Prescribe la fe asociada con Dámaso de Roma y Pedro de Alejandría y amenaza a quienes clasifica como disidentes. Una prescripción no demuestra aceptación inmediata ni cumplimiento uniforme. Esta reconstrucción sigue preparativos y entregas locales ficticios; el destinatario distante permanece fuera del mapa.

dramatizationNotice.en: Working contexts, local products, seven original identities, courts, resource shares and conversations are invented. They are not imperial autographs or a measured enforcement network. The later Codex is a source for the modern reconstruction, never a fifth-century book placed on a desk in 380. No order makes historical faith, dissent or population acceptance a scored resource.
dramatizationNotice.es-ES: Los contextos de trabajo, productos locales, siete identidades originales, patios, asignaciones y conversaciones son inventados. No son autógrafos imperiales ni una red comprobada de cumplimiento. El Código posterior es fuente de la reconstrucción moderna, nunca un libro del siglo V colocado en una mesa de 380. Ninguna orden convierte la fe histórica, la disidencia o la aceptación de la población en un recurso puntuable.

text.en: On 27 February 380 a constitution was issued at Thessalonica in the names of Gratian, Valentinian and Theodosius. Its heading addresses the people of Constantinople. It prescribes the faith associated with Damasus of Rome and Peter of Alexandria and threatens those it classifies as dissenters. A prescription is not evidence of immediate acceptance or uniform enforcement. This reconstruction follows fictional local preparation and handovers; the distant addressee remains outside the map.
text.es-ES: El 27 de febrero de 380 se emitió en Tesalónica una constitución en nombre de Graciano, Valentiniano y Teodosio. Su encabezamiento se dirige al pueblo de Constantinopla. Prescribe la fe asociada con Dámaso de Roma y Pedro de Alejandría y amenaza a quienes clasifica como disidentes. Una prescripción no demuestra aceptación inmediata ni cumplimiento uniforme. Esta reconstrucción sigue preparativos y entregas locales ficticios; el destinatario distante permanece fuera del mapa.

en: Marcus is forty-six. In his invented later clerical life he receives a report of the constitution; he does not attend its drafting or issue. His ordinary remembered conversation is fiction, not an
ancient quotation.
es-ES: Marco tiene cuarenta y seis años. En su vida administrativa posterior inventada recibe noticias de la constitución; no asiste a su redacción ni emisión. Su conversación cotidiana recordada es ficción, no una

text.en: A younger copyist tapped the three names at the top and asked whether that made three witnesses. I nearly gave him the easy answer. Instead I turned the sheet and asked him to mark where it had been issued and whom it addressed. He found two cities. He looked annoyed; I remembered being his age. My own hand had begun to ache before the morning work was finished.
text.es-ES: Un copista más joven señaló los tres nombres del encabezamiento y preguntó si eso hacía tres testigos. Estuve a punto de darle la respuesta fácil. En cambio, giré la hoja y le pedí que señalara dónde se había emitido y a quién se dirigía. Encontró dos ciudades. Pareció fastidiado; recordé mi propia juventud. A mí ya me dolía la mano antes de acabar el trabajo de la mañana.

Ninguna orden convierte la fe histórica, la disidencia o la aceptación de la población en un recurso puntuable.

event.en: In late 380, Theodosius entered Constantinople and ordered changes in church possession. Socrates places the arrival and transfer on separate November days; Marcellinus records the restoration he favored in December. These later accounts do not establish what every inhabitant believed. The following local service story is invented.

Sócrates sitúa la llegada y el traspaso en días distintos de noviembre; Marcelino fecha en diciembre la restauración que favorecía. Estos relatos posteriores no establecen qué creía cada habitante. La siguiente historia asistencial local es inventada.

failureRecovery.beforeCommit: Preview is free. An unaffordable confirmation changes no account. A complete reserved plan can be cancelled before irreversible commitment, refunding only its escrow; compare and reserve again.
failureRecovery.afterCommit: Costs are paid once and methods remain locked. An incorrect destination or absent recipient creates no service receipt: direct the same living original output and recipients to the selected court and obtain fresh observations. No timer substitutes for work or arrival.
failureRecovery.mainIdentityLoss: Loss of a required original recipient, loss of the selected worker before recorded work, or destruction of a genuinely generated selected output causes defeat under the existing reference rules. No free resurrection or hidden grace period is promised. A worker lost after recorded work adds no new worker-return condition.
failureRecovery.optionalIdentityLoss: Only the corresponding optional fails; no main defeat, late reward or campaign restart. Main victory closes unfinished optionals.
failureRecovery.resources: At least one complete plan remains affordable in each difficulty with all optionals skipped. Optional stock and protected recovery cannot fund the main reservation; there is no gathering, regeneration, passive income or replacement purchase in this reference design.
failureRecovery.nativeStatus: All recovery descriptions still require native input/template, save/load and game checks; reference behavior alone is not an engine implementation.

cases: For each difficulty, enumerate all nine complete recipe selections and distinguish the 9/7/3 affordable rows without counting optional rewards.
For every affordable selection, test reserve, cancel before commitment and irreversible commitment with exact selected costs, preserving all isolated account balances.
Payment or shared attendance alone must not complete either selected service. Confirm selected work, genuine generation, correct output and original recipient reception separately.
At final evaluation require the selected output and original living recipients freshly present at that recipe's own court; reject wrong recipe, stale receipt, substitute or wrong court.
Observe simultaneous required loss and potential victory in both input orders; required defeat must win. Preserve valid recorded work when only its former worker is lost afterward.
Skip all seven secondaries and complete the main plan in each difficulty; separately test all-complete and the three authored portfolios with actual travel and reachable payment prefixes.
On Hard, shared-hearth plus rented shelter leaves 20 wood: repair cannot pay its 50-wood cost before suitable earned aid; no reward may pay its own prerequisite debit.

Verify all nineteen point centres, ten main circles and full widths of all twenty-one connections against terrain/building footprints; modern coastline clearance alone cannot pass land or ancient geography.
Save/load before and after reservation, cancellation, commitment, each work/generation/reception, each optional reward and final terminal evaluation.
Verify the 51 authored screen records in EN/es-ES, factual-to-personal opening, disputed dates, service choice and clear unaffordable/cancel/commit/recovery messages.
Complete this intermediate episode and recommend only the existing 381 council finale; do not write campaign completion or offer successor campaigns early.

playstyles.costOfOpportunity: Make the two distinct aid deliveries before paying the damaged-store repair where the remaining wood cannot fund it. This costs a separate northern circuit and attention before or alongside service work; the payment is never the repair itself.

Visit the authored viewpoints and observe existing service destinations before choosing routes. Information takes movement and attention but creates no new road, speed bonus, ancient landmark or military advantage.

Return the separate consenting optional household identities and compare the attributed source accounts. Neither action replaces a main recipient, decides the disputed date or changes church possession.

gameplayIdentity.problem: Choose one meal method and one shelter method under finite joint accounts, then perform their actual selected work and receptions for distinct fictional original people.
gameplayIdentity.decision: Compare resource composition, local travel and optional information/aid before irreversible commitment. The 9/7/3 affordable sets provide increasingly constrained choices without a fabricated riot, clock or enemy army.
gameplayIdentity.density: Nineteen local places, six work/output methods, three shelter receiving courts, one meal court and seven distinct optional tasks; avoid making the giant frame a compulsory empty walking tour.
gameplayIdentity.replay: The historical possession change remains fixed. Replay varies the chosen pair, approach/return routes and the three combinable optional portfolios.
gameplayIdentity.pacing: Reflective civic episode between the Thessalonica law and the 381 council finale. Hard is an uncalibrated allocation/travel hypothesis; fewer workers and waiting are not advertised as the challenge.
gameplayIdentity.limits: No measured duration or native difficulty approval; conduct full-width navigation and per-difficulty playtests before mechanical historical authoring.

text.en: In late 380, Theodosius entered Constantinople and ordered changes in church possession. Socrates places the arrival and transfer on separate November days; Marcellinus records the restoration he favored in December. These later accounts do not establish what every inhabitant believed. The following local service story is invented.
text.es-ES: A finales de 380, Teodosio entró en Constantinopla y ordenó cambios en la posesión de iglesias. Sócrates sitúa la llegada y el traspaso en días distintos de noviembre; Marcelino fecha en diciembre la restauración que favorecía. Estos relatos posteriores no establecen qué creía cada habitante. La siguiente historia asistencial local es inventada.

event.en: In 381 a council at Constantinople reaffirmed Nicene faith. Its transmitted canons address religious teaching, territorial administration and the city’s honorary rank after Rome as New Rome. These provisions did not instantly end disagreement or create today’s denominations. Later letters and the surviving transmission of the associated creed require their own dates. Our local reconstruction separates three working contexts before the campaign offers a choice of historical perspective.
event.es-ES: En 381 un concilio de Constantinopla reafirmó la fe nicena. Sus cánones transmitidos tratan enseñanza religiosa, administración territorial y rango honorífico de la ciudad tras Roma como Nueva Roma. Esas disposiciones no terminaron de inmediato con los desacuerdos ni crearon las confesiones actuales. Las cartas posteriores y la transmisión conservada del credo asociado requieren sus propias fechas. Nuestra reconstrucción local separa tres contextos de trabajo antes de ofrecer una elección de perspectiva histórica.

historicalOutcome.en: The three fictional local indexes and their distinct work shares are recorded. They do not reenact a council vote, prove universal reception or decide which later church is true. The Eagle and the Cross ends its selected frame in 381. Your chosen western or eastern perspective recommends an independent successor campaign. Both return to 337 and revisit part of this history through another narrator.
historicalOutcome.es-ES: Quedan registrados los tres índices locales ficticios y sus asignaciones distintas de trabajo. No reproducen una votación conciliar, prueban recepción universal ni deciden qué iglesia posterior es verdadera. El águila y la cruz termina su marco seleccionado en 381. Tu perspectiva elegida, occidental u oriental, recomienda una campaña sucesora independiente. Ambas vuelven a 337 y revisitan parte de esta historia con otro narrador.
